summary: Iter 53 — Verified the new allocation-categories UX, the approved-user allocation guard, and the cookie-banner admin auto-hide. Backend: 8/8 pytest passed in 40s (/app/backend/tests/test_iter53_categories_guard.py). Seeded 4 test verification_submissions directly in Mongo (needs_review-complete, verified, rejected, needs_review-missing) and cleaned them all up. GET /api/admin/allocate/categories returns the 6 required buckets (pending_unassigned, pending_assigned, missing_details, no_verification, approved, rejected) each with count/items/allocatable/hint; allocatable flags correct (true only for pending_* and missing_details). POST /api/admin/allocate returns HTTP 400 with detail 'Some selected users are not awaiting review (approved, rejected or never applied) and cannot be allocated.' whenever submission_ids contains a verified/rejected doc — even when mixed with a valid needs_review id NOTHING is written (verified the needs_review doc still has assigned_to=None after the failing call, so the guard is all-or-nothing). POST /api/admin/allocate with category='missing_details' and no submission_ids correctly allocates ONLY the missing-details pending sub (the complete pending sub stays untouched) and the verified/rejected docs are never touched. RBAC: sub-admin X-Staff-Token gets 403 on GET /admin/allocate/categories AND POST /admin/allocate (regression preserved from iter52). Frontend E2E (Playwright, main admin admin@vametra.com/Shiv@12345): Users tab → Allocate opens the panel with 6 chips + counts (pending_unassigned 0, pending_assigned 1, missing_details 1, no_verification 2, approved 0, rejected 3). Clicking a non-allocatable chip (approved/no_verification/rejected) shows [data-testid=allocate-blocked-note], disables the submit CTA, and marks every allocate-user-* row disabled — verified individually for all three. Clicking pending_unassigned / missing_details hides the blocked note and shows candidates (missing_details row shows amber 'Missing: Contact number' hint on Vaibhav Deshmane). Cookie banner: with localStorage cleared the banner IS visible on public '/' but is NOT rendered on /admin-login or /admin-cms — the users table bottom rows are no longer covered. isAdminArea gate in CookieConsent.jsx (/^\/admin/ + isStaff()) works correctly.
action_items: None blocking — categories UX, allocation guard, and cookie-banner admin auto-hide all working as specified.

Nice-to-have: the 'Select all N' button is only shown for allocatable categories that have items; if pending_unassigned count is 0 it disappears. Consider a tiny 'Nothing pending' inline hint on the button strip so main admin knows the queue is empty (currently the empty candidates area with 'No users in this category' already covers this, so cosmetic only).

Nice-to-have: the AllocatePanel chip selector uses data-testid prefix 'allocate-cat-' which also matches the cat-hint element (data-testid=allocate-cat-hint). Consider renaming the hint to 'allocate-cathint' or 'allocate-hint' so prefix-based queries (as used by pytests / automation) don't include the hint node. Non-blocking (tests can filter it out).
critical_code_review_comments: subadmin.allocate(): the 400-eligibility check counts eligible docs but does not distinguish which specific ids are invalid — the error message is generic. Fine for MVP; consider returning the offending submission_ids in the detail for a better admin UX.

subadmin.allocation_categories(): the 'missing_details' bucket is a SUBSET of pending_unassigned + pending_assigned (a pending sub with missing fields is counted in TWO buckets). The chip counts therefore do not sum to total submissions — intentional but worth documenting so admins don't get confused when totals appear to overlap.

CookieConsent.jsx isAdminArea gate uses pathname regex /^\/admin/ which correctly matches /admin, /admin-login, /admin-cms, and /admin/*. Good. Also OR-ed with isStaff() so if a sub-admin JWT lives in localStorage but they are on '/' the banner is still suppressed — matches the spec wording 'staff session exists'.

subadmin._missing_details() treats missing documents (neither selfie_file_id nor document_file_id) as a missing detail even though the pipeline usually requires those before status flips to needs_review. Not incorrect, but if some legacy submissions were force-flipped to needs_review without files they'll all land in missing_details — acceptable and even desirable.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 53 sealed the allocation-only-for-pending guard and the categories view. The endpoint POST /api/admin/allocate is now truly all-or-nothing: any non-needs_review id anywhere in submission_ids => 400 and no writes. GET /api/admin/allocate/categories returns 6 buckets keyed pending_unassigned, pending_assigned, missing_details, no_verification, approved, rejected — the first three are allocatable, the last three are read-only. Cookie banner is suppressed for any pathname starting /admin OR when a staff JWT session exists (isStaff()==true), so future admin screens automatically inherit the fix. Regression suites of interest: /app/backend/tests/test_iter51_subadmin.py, test_iter52_phaseb_allocation.py, test_iter53_categories_guard.py.
